questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Honestly I really wanted to have an exchange in country with warmer weather than Denmark. I also really wanted to try surfing, and Portugal seemed like an obvious choice. It was a bonus that Nova is a super nice and ambitious school.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Not too difficult. There was a SharePoint page where most of the information needed could be found.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I did not really receive any assistance, but I don't think I needed much either.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: The course selection, which is an auction, is super weird. No information is given regarding previous bids, and Erasmus Master students receive less than freemovers and I heard of no-one that got all the courses that they wanted. I did however receive an extra course from the exchange office when I was 3,5 ECTS short.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was offered a room by a friend of mine who studied in Lisbon the semester prior to mine. I would recommend finding people who have studied in Lisbon previously and have them add you to WhatsApp groups where (mostly german) students are renting out rooms constantly.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: While my commute was a bit long (1-1,5 hours) from Northern Lisbon - I would have found it much too boring to live on or near campus. The metro and train work very well - the busses are awful, don't trust them. Everything, except surfing, happens in the city in my experience.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I heard mixed reviews. I think the key tip is to start searching early.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: It is an auction where you bid for courses. I like the concept, but in practice it does not work very well.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: You can't really see any of the courses available before you are added to the SharePoint (1-2 weeks before the semester). No information is given regarding previous bids, and Erasmus Master students receive less points to bid than freemovers and I heard of no-one that got all the courses that they wanted. I did however receive an extra course from the exchange office when I was 3,5 ECTS short.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 1 course from my pre-approved courses. I ended up having pretty random courses in somewhat annoying timeslots.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Just pick courses from last years selection for your pre-approval and grant applications. You are most likely going to have to adjust your courses afterwards.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Academic level was a little below UCPH, but much more group-work and group assignments (which requires you to be on campus).

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I found it to be slightly below that of UCPH.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Much more group-work and group assignments (which requires you to be on campus). Nothing is recorded.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Banking - 7 ECTS
Development Economics - 7 ECTS
International Business - 3,5 ECTS
Quality Management - 3,5 ECTS
Big Data Analysis - 3,5 ECTS
Energy and Climate Change - 3,5 ECTS
Marketing Analytics - 3,5 ECTS

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Big Data Analysis was super interesting, if you're into that sort of stuff. It simulated a Formula 1 race as a way to grade students and the programming language was super easy to use.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Uber and Bolt is so cheap (taxi on your phone), it becomes addicting to use it. I spent much more on restaurant and cafe visits than expected, due to it being very affordable.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Restaurants, wine, drinks, beer was much cheaper that expected. Shopping at the super market was more expensive than expected.
I could have burritos delivered to my door from HOY! for 8 Euros - that ended up being a large cost in the end.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Did not really use these. I know there was football practice sometimes.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There was a bunch of clubs you could sign up for, but I did not feel i could contribute meaningfully in a single semester. Check
https://www.novasbe.unl.pt/en/life-at-nova-sbe/nova-way-of-life

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Surfing. I loved it and Nova has a deal with Lisbon Surf Camp meaning you can have 4 lessons and 8 rental sessions in a month for 50 EUR which is insanely cheap.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
Go to Madeira with friends, it is an amazing island with stunning views. 
Go to Sintra (preferably on a week day due to tourists), Porto and Algarve coast for culture and views. 
I recommend Caparica, Guincho, Peniche and Ericeira for surfing. Try to catch a WSL event.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Eating dinner late and therefore going to class later was no problem. Everyone was very friendly, I found.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It is a little hard to connect with local students to be honest. Lots of Erasmus students though. The portugues students I befriended was through randomly assigned groups in course assignment work.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: You pretty much need cash with you at all time which is a little annoying but no big deal. I found that everything takes a significant longer amount of time and no-one seems to mind - it is very common to wait for drink order and payment at the grocery store for long.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
The local openness and the "we're gonna make it, don't worry" attitude is super refreshing. 
I really liked the surfing culture as well amongst us beginners - locals will yell at you in the water though.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Live in the city and get a public transport card. 
Try surfing - it's so much fun (Nova has a locker for boards and wetsuits right next to the ocean)
Go to restaurants as much as possible

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Apply for a bunch of grants and scholarships - the pay per hour of just getting one is extremely high.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Going on trips with friends I made in Portugal was super nice. I went to a bunch of places, both with international and fellow countrymen - most of which I have spent time with afterwards too!

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Honestly the auction part and getting the courses I needed to cover 30 ECTS was a struggle. I guess meeting Portuguese people was a challenge too.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
